title: Comparing Your Real Options for Selling Digital Art Without PayPal — No Stripe Required
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: If you’re a digital creator in Nigeria, Pakistan, or Ghana, Stripe and PayPal’s country restrictions lock you out of selling your art, ebooks, or templates globally. Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, and Paddle follow suit, leaving you with no platform to process payments or deliver products. The problem isn’t your work—it’s the architecture. Conventional platforms rent you access to payment rails they control. Sovereign commerce infrastructure flips this: you own the stack, the payment logic, the delivery mechanism. This post compares your real options for selling digital products without relying on platforms that exclude your country. We’ll analyze tradeoffs, costs, and ownership—then show you how to deploy a stack no platform can take from you.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Conventional platforms like Gumroad or Paddle offer simplicity: upload your product, set a price, and share a link. They handle payment processing, file delivery, and customer support—but only if your country is on their approved list. Workarounds like using a VPN or proxy to access Stripe or PayPal are temporary and violate terms of service, risking account suspension. Sovereign commerce stacks, in contrast, give you full ownership of the infrastructure. GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages host your storefront for free. Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script handle backend logic. Supabase or Google Sheets store orders. NOWPayments verifies crypto payments on-chain. You own every layer, so no platform can restrict your access. The tradeoff? You must configure the stack once. The reward? Permanent infrastructure sovereignty.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms like Stripe and PayPal exclude countries based on regulatory, financial, or political risk—not your ability to sell. Nigeria, Ghana, and Pakistan are blocked due to perceived fraud risk, currency instability, or lack of local banking partnerships. Even if you use a workaround, these platforms can freeze your account or withhold funds without warning. Sovereign stacks bypass this entirely. NOWPayments processes 300+ cryptocurrencies with no KYC, no buyer account required, and a flat 0.5% fee. Recommended networks like BSC, Solana, or TRON keep transaction fees under $0.10. The stack runs on globally accessible infrastructure like GitHub and Cloudflare, so no single entity can restrict your access. The architecture is pressure-tested in Zimbabwe, where currency collapse and financial isolation are the norm—not the exception.

Platforms like Gumroad charge 10% per sale. PayPal and Stripe take 2.9% + $0.30 per transaction—if they’re available. Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

With platforms, you rent access to tools you don’t control. If they change their terms, raise fees, or shut down, your business is at risk. Sovereign stacks give you full ownership of the codebase, the payment logic, and the delivery mechanism. Google Drive or Cloudflare R2 stores your files for free. Cloudflare Workers automates order fulfillment the moment payment confirms. The stack is deployed to your GitHub or Cloudflare account—COREMERCH has no access after delivery. This is infrastructure sovereignty: you own the tools, the data, and the process. No platform can restrict your access, freeze your funds, or change the rules mid-game. The architecture is built for permanence, not convenience.
